evidence.quote:
Thank you for the opportunity to review this open letter entitled, “Integrating ethical and legal
frameworks in multi hazard disaster risk management.” As it is an open Letter not a research article,
it therefore has a different focus. I provide this feedback based on the criteria and guidelines for
reviewing an open letter.
1. Is the rationale for the Open Letter provided in sufficient detail?
The rationale for the open letter was not fully apparent to me in the abstract or the document
itself. The objective of the open letter appears to be to critically evaluate the success of an
integrated Decision Support System (DSS) developed by the European MEDiate project. But at
various stages when reading the article I felt that it did not provide much of a critical lens, and was
instead written in a descriptive and promotional style to explain the benefits of the DSS system. I
also wasn't sure about the author's standpoint and whether they had some involvement in the
creation of the DSS system that is the subject of the article.
My main critical and constructive feedback relates to the structure of the article. I think it could
benefit from a restructure that brings forward the literature review sections, which are provided in
the latter part of the paper (part 5). Then a more coherent structure might be: (a) identify the
problem or issue under consideration; (b) state a methodology for critical analysis, informed by
the literature review, and then (c) apply the literature to the case study (DSS system) to determine
whether or not it is meeting the objectives, namely, the integration of ethical and human rights
frameworks into multi-hazard DRM. This is where the differing national frameworks and
approaches can be introduced, together with key challenges and emerging trends.
2. Does the article adequately reference differing views and opinions?
It was very interesting to read about the different national frameworks in MEDiate testbed
countries. This was an enjoyable part of the paper that gives context to its overall objective.
However, again to structure, I think introducing the national frameworks after the literature
review would foreground the evidence against which the DSS system can be evaluated in relation




to the national frameworks provided.
3. Are all factual statements correct, and are statements and arguments made adequately
supported by citations?
For a piece of this length that draws upon a large body of disaster risk management literature, it is
considerably under-cited. Citations are often not provided where they ought to be. An example is
on page 8 in part 5.2, where the author states, “Studies highlight that many failures in disaster
coordination stem from different agencies and systems being unable to seamlessly share data
and models.” A statement such as this requires a citation to point the reader to the evidence (the
studies) that it refers to. At this stage I do not consider that this article satisfies the criteria that all
factual statements are correct and adequately supported by citations.
4. Is the Open Letter written in accessible language?
Yes, the language is accessible. There is a repetitive paragraph on Page 3. The second paragraph
in Part 2 almost repeats verbatim the preceding paragraph and should be deleted. There also
appears to be a typographical error on page 8 where the Covid-19 pandemic sentence says
‘…international organisations advising against traying rights through public health measures.’ Is
this meant to say betraying?
5. Where applicable, are recommendations and next steps explained clearly for others to follow?
Yes, section 6 offers some suggestions for how MEDiate DSS can become more participatory, and
it also identifies future research avenues. Section 6 covers a lot of good analytical ground that
could be drawn out earlier in the article, applied to the case study and through the national
frameworks, and not left right to the end.
Overall, this is a very interesting article on an important topic that shows promise. With some
restructuring it would achieve more clarity and coherence. Closer attention to citation is also
required.
Thank you for the opportunity to provide feedback.

Dear reviewer, Thank you very much for your insightful and constructive feedback, which I
found highly valuable in revising the Open Letter. Here is how I have addressed your
comments:
Clarifying the Objective and Standpoint: I revised the Introduction to make the
critical stance clearer, explaining that the Open Letter offers a preliminary critical
reflection on MEDiate's ambitions and early development, while noting my
involvement as an external analyst (not as a DSS system developer).
Restructuring the Document: Following your recommendation, I restructured the
paper to move the critical literature discussion (previously in Part 5) earlier in the text,
now immediately following the introduction of the problem and before the discussion
of national frameworks and case studies. This restructuring strengthens the
analytical lens applied to the DSS throughout the document.
Citation Improvements: I conducted a full review and added numerous citations to
substantiate all major factual assertions, especially in the literature review and when
referring to disaster coordination failures and rights-based disaster response models.
Removing Repetitions and Typographical Errors: I deleted the redundant
paragraph in Section 2 and corrected the typographical error you spotted (changing
"traying rights" to "betraying rights" in the COVID-19 sentence).
Bringing Analytical Points Earlier: Drawing on your advice, I brought forward some
of the critical reflections originally reserved for Section 6 (on challenges and future
directions) and integrated them earlier in the case study analysis. This approach
ensures that the evaluation of MEDiate's integration of ethics and rights frameworks
is more consistently threaded throughout the document.
I am truly grateful for your careful reading and your suggestions, which greatly improved
the clarity, coherence, and scholarly robustness of the Open Letter.
